waterbodyNames: Malolos River Districts (Atlag, Panasahan, and Calero; proposal lead only)
question: Do newly surfaced freshwater sources provide locality-resolved wild fish records for Bulacan, or only aquaculture/ecosystem context?

reviewedSources.title: Plankton Community Structure of the Aquaculture Ponds in Marilao and Meycauayan, Bulacan, Philippines

fieldScopeAsReported.waterSourceContext: Fishponds using effluent/water from the Marilao-Meycauayan-Obando River System.
fieldScopeAsReported.methodsSummary: Freshwater plankton was collected by approximately 3 m horizontal surface tows with a 64-micron mesh net, then identified and enumerated.

fishEvidenceDisposition.dietEvidence: The article describes plankton generally as primary fish food, but reports no fish species, stomach-content analysis, or species-specific diet observations.
fishEvidenceDisposition.decision: Use only as attributed fishpond plankton/ecosystem context. Do not turn its plankton taxa into fish occurrences, river records, or species-specific diet claims.

reuse.access: Publisher-hosted article PDF and indexed text reviewed; no local copy or table image retained.
reuse.itemSpecificTerms: No article-specific license or permission was verified during this review.

reviewedSources.title: Assessment of the Effect of Remediation Strategies on the Environmental Quality of Aquaculture Ponds in Marilao and Meycauayan, Bulacan, Philippines

fieldScopeAsReported.organismEvidence: The experiment reports stocked and cultured milkfish (Chanos chanos) and tracks growth, survival, feed conversion, and contaminants. It is a pond-remediation/aquaculture experiment, not a wild fish survey.
fieldScopeAsReported.decision: Do not project cultured milkfish as naturally occurring in either river, and do not use pond growth/feed results as a natural-diet record or food-safety advice.

reuse.access: PubMed/PMC article metadata and indexed full-text content reviewed.
reuse.itemSpecificTerms: No article-specific license was confirmed in this bounded review.

rejectedRetrievalLead.titleAsDisplayed: Morphometric Traits of Ichthyofauna in Malolos District Rivers, Bulacan, Philippines Year 2021
rejectedRetrievalLead.hostedPageTitle: CARPIO, Carl Lawrence R. - Module 4 Answer Sheet
screenFindings: The surfaced text is embedded in a third-party-hosted school module/answer-sheet upload, not an official repository copy of a completed fish survey.

The displayed fish-research section states objectives and research questions in proposal/future tense and says there are no journals or scientific papers describing Malolos river ichthyofauna; no methods, results, fish names, collection events, or specimen evidence were exposed.

A broad web search for the exact title, author, named Atlag/Panasahan/Calero river districts, and school/government domains found no independent completed-study copy. This bounded search does not prove that no copy exists elsewhere.
rejectedRetrievalLead.decision: Retrieval lead only; exclude from fish inventory, occurrence, taxonomy, geometry, diet, and app data unless an authoritative completed report with methods and results is located.

evidenceDecision.decision: The peer-reviewed pond studies improve freshwater aquaculture and plankton context but add no wild fish checklist for the rivers. The Malolos item is a proposal-only retrieval lead. Keep all three lanes distinct, and continue searching for locality-resolved, method-described Bulacan wild-fish surveys.

limitations: Fishponds that use river water are not the same sampling habitat as the river channel; stocked species do not prove wild occurrence.
A general statement that plankton can be fish food is not a species-specific diet observation.
The 2018 and 2022 pond studies are separate objectives and dates but share an author and study locations; they are not independent wild-fish surveys.
No current species presence, capture location, river geometry, fishing access, safety, legality, natural diet, or bait recommendation is established by this screen.
This review does not establish absence of fish studies or species from Bulacan.
nextStep: Continue L3 discovery with primary, site-resolved Bulacan river and lake studies or public specimen datasets. Keep farmed, wild-capture, interview, plankton, and water-quality evidence in separate lanes; retain Central Luzon and Luzon as incomplete.
